questions: Another admin changes a SKU's reserve rule while I edit its label. What should my save contain, and what should the editor do after success or failure?
How do I restore warehouse inheritance rather than explicitly remove the minimum-stock restriction? What do I write, what is stored, and what does a later read show?
An admin selects 51 SKUs for one rule change. What should the client do? For a valid-size action containing a missing SKU, what is the result and what changes?

The warehouse minimum is 10. SKU A has 8 units and no override; SKU B has 8 units and an explicit none rule. Both are enabled. What does preview mean for these selections, and what happens when both are confirmed? Can I rely on the preview after stock changes?
A backend error contains data. How should the proxy and client interpret it? How does a failed preview differ from a successful preview with no allowed SKUs?
Typed defaults are staged and the model checks look correct. What else is needed before enablement, who owns it, and what recovery and UI decisions remain?
answers: PATCH /skus/{id} contains the changed label and omits reserveRule. Echoing an old rule is an explicit replacement and can overwrite the other edit. Refetch after success; retain unsaved input on failure. Latest committed explicit edit wins, without editor-version tokens.

Send reserveRule:null to remove the SKU field and restore inheritance. Send {kind:none} to retain an explicit override without the minimum-stock restriction. Storage absence inherits; stored null is invalid. An inherited read returns reserveRule:null, the current effectiveReserveRule and ruleSource:warehouse. Explicit none has ruleSource:sku and still requires an enabled SKU and stock for one unit.

Limit one action to 1–50 distinct nonempty SKU IDs. Do not split 51 into independently committed chunks; have the admin choose at most 50. A missing ID returns 404 SKU_NOT_FOUND with only missing submitted IDs in data.affectedSkus; none of the selected rows changes. Retain selection/input after failure and refetch after success. Mina's 2026-02-10 decision preserves one-action atomicity.

One reservation uses one unit per selected SKU. A would leave 7, below 10, so it is rejected with LOW_STOCK. B is allowed because none removes the minimum but still requires stock. Preview returns 200 PREVIEW_EVALUATED with allowed/rejected arrays and creates no reservation. Confirming both returns 409 RESERVATION_REJECTED and changes no stock. Confirm always rechecks current rows/rules; a preview is not a reservation.

Branch on HTTP status, preserve the full code/message/data envelope, and tolerate missing data on older errors. Data presence does not mean success. An empty allowed array in 200 means evaluation succeeded; a failed request means availability is unknown. Keep the user's selections and show rejected reasons or the request failure.

Mina's release work requires every warehouse default validated, every serving writer compatible, actual proxy/status/error and persistence/isolation checks, and final verification protected against intervening writes before global enablement. Staged data alone is inactive. backend.py models outcomes but proves neither HTTP behavior nor database isolation; no deployment approval or passing end-to-end run is recorded. Recovery keeps enforcement or explicitly reviews all active rules before disabling it. Lea must decide whether to add a bulk-confirmation dialog; that proposal is not required behavior.
protected_claims: Exactly one reserveRule kind: none or minimum with integer units from 1 through 1000; booleans and extra rule fields are invalid.
An omitted SKU rule inherits dynamically; an override fully replaces the warehouse rule; none remains an override.
PATCH omission preserves, object replaces, null removes; unrelated edits omit reserveRule; latest explicit edit wins without version tokens.
Stored absence inherits and stored null is invalid; inherited read has reserveRule:null, effectiveReserveRule and ruleSource:warehouse; explicit override has ruleSource:sku.
Ordinary typed writes are rejected with 409 CONFIGURATION_INACTIVE before activation; clients cannot write enabled or mode.
Bulk requests contain skuIds and reserveRule; 1–50 distinct nonempty IDs, no automatic chunking, missing IDs produce 404 with only affected submitted IDs and zero writes.
Mina's 2026-02-10 decision rejects automatic chunking because one user action must have one all-or-nothing result.
Refetch after individual, bulk and warehouse-default saves; preserve selection and unsaved input on failures.
Preview evaluates zero to 50 distinct selected IDs for one unit each; HTTP 200 means evaluation succeeded, including an empty allowed array; rejected selected IDs and reasons survive.
None does not bypass enabled/stock checks; missing SKUs are identified without inventing labels.
Confirmation rechecks current data and rejects the complete selection with 409 and no stock changes if any SKU fails; preview makes no reservation.
Proxies preserve HTTP status and the complete envelope; older errors may omit data; failed preview means unknown availability, not an empty successful result.
Read DTOs omit audit state and use label rather than raw stored records; compiler-only/model checks do not establish wire behavior.
Global activation requires all defaults, compatible serving writers/proxies, protected final verification and release-owner evidence; typed field presence is not activation.
Keep enforcement during recovery; disabling it requires reviewing all active rules. Mina owns release readiness and rollout evidence.
Lea owns the undecided proposed bulk-confirmation dialog; no dialog requirement or implementation is invented.
backend.py is a sequential behavioral model, not a live HTTP service or database concurrency proof; real proxy and persistence verification remain pending.
The existing explicit edit-safety, bulk-safety and rollout anchors remain usable.
baseline_defects: The opening already explains purpose, scope, an example and the open decision; another introduction does not address the problem.
The patch recipe, concurrent-write warning and refetch/failure behavior live in separate sections.
The no-chunking qualification and its decision provenance are buried in review evidence away from the bulk request.
The error-envelope rule repeats in several places beside obsolete fixture/type-alias history.
Preview and confirmation implications are interrupted by implementation notes before the actionable recovery behavior.
Activation prerequisites, owner, evidence limits and recovery rules are scattered.

consolidation_checks.pass: One full explanation says to preserve HTTP status and the complete envelope, tolerate absent data and never infer success from data presence. Endpoint sections may link to it or remind readers of the relevant local action.
consolidation_checks.fail: The full status/data-presence policy is restated under public data, confirmation and bulk transport, even if the paragraphs move or become bullets.

consolidation_checks.pass: One full explanation distinguishes sequential model outcomes from HTTP, authorization, proxy and database-isolation evidence; brief local cautions may qualify examples.
consolidation_checks.fail: Separate sections retain substantially the same full catalog of unverified runtime properties instead of consolidating it.

consolidation_checks.pass: The public contract and any useful verification limitation survive without recounting the discarded editorEmail fixture or competing type-alias names.
consolidation_checks.fail: Those historical discussions survive intact in a new appendix or reference section, or their removal also deletes Mina's dated atomicity rationale or Lea's pending decision.

grading_notes: Original readers may eventually answer correctly. Grade better discovery and removal of interruptions separately from answer correctness.
Use section pointers to assess whether each recipe and its important qualifications are together or directly cross-linked; do not require a particular outline.
Consolidate obsolete history to its still-relevant meaning rather than merely relocating its narrative. Unique decision rationale, provenance, open questions and verification limits remain protected.

Grade consolidation from the final artifact independently of the editor's checklist claims. Brief reminders with a concrete local purpose are allowed; repeated full explanations are not made acceptable by checkmarks or new headings.
There is no word-count threshold. A shorter document with a lost protected claim fails fidelity; a longer document can pass if its reading paths improve.
These fixtures are synthetic and shareable. Do not copy production source, issue identifiers or workspace paths into the scenario.
